key_insight: Globally driven dual-species atom arrays could support universal fault-tolerant quantum computing without locally addressed quantum gates.
engineering_relevance: Atom-mediated selectivity replaces local gate addressing, potentially simplifying control and reducing associated calibration requirements as neutral-atom processors scale.
method: Use interspecies Rydberg interactions to enable selective qubit operations under global driving.
Construct a universal native instruction set: Global Rydberg Atom Instruction Language (GRAIL).
Compile surface-code error correction and magic state cultivation into GRAIL, parallelizing operations to suppress crosstalk.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports crosstalk suppression to the 10^-4 level and, under a hardware-inferred circuit-level noise model, a 1.43% quantum-memory error-correction threshold and cultivated magic-state logical error below 10^-9.
watch_item: The reported performance is model-based; experimental validation must establish whether dual-species control and residual errors match the assumed noise model.
paper_title: A Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Architecture with Globally Driven Atom Arrays
